title: BYOC Cloud and SIP trunks
summary: Carrier and PBX trunks, RTP over the internet, Dynamic Cloud Voice, and the quick-start order.

lessons.title: BYOC Cloud is your carrier, Genesys’ media
lessons.summary: You bring the carrier contract. Genesys terminates a SIP trunk on the AWS media tier. Audio is RTP on the internet.
paras: The overview says you create the trunk in Telephony Admin between Genesys Cloud media resources in AWS and a third-party carrier or device. That far end can be another cloud or a box on prem, but it needs a public address and open ports. There is no customer Edge hardware in the pure BYOC Cloud path.

Because RTP crosses the public internet, the overview tells you to judge latency and loss before you commit. Genesys Cloud Voice is the other choice: Genesys is the carrier, including emergency services on numbers you buy there. Mixing them does not copy emergency data from Genesys Cloud Voice into your BYOC carrier.

lessons.title: Carrier trunks and PBX trunks
lessons.summary: BYOC Carrier and BYOC PBX are the two types. Carrier has subtypes. PBX has one.
paras: The create-trunk article lists BYOC Carrier and BYOC PBX. Carrier subtypes called out there are Generic BYOC Carrier, Genesys Cloud BYOC Verizon, and BYOC WhatsApp Business Calling. PBX has a single subtype. Start from the base settings. Open the advanced sections only when the carrier’s questionnaire says you must.

WhatsApp as a trunk subtype is not the same object as an inbound message flow. One is telephony signaling for WhatsApp Business Calling. The other is Architect routing for messages. Do not collapse them because the brand name matches.

lessons.title: The quick-start order
lessons.summary: Location, trunk, outbound route, number plan. The product on the subscription comes before all of that.
paras: The quick start’s order is the lab’s order. Confirm the org and that BYOC Cloud is on the subscription. Work the carrier requirements. Add a physical location. Create the trunk. Assign it on an outbound route. Genesys creates default outbound routes and still requires you to attach the trunk. Add or adjust number plans for the classifications you dial.

The location is also the emergency story. Skipping it to “test the SIP first” leaves 911 with nowhere honest to point. New trunks should be Dynamic Cloud Voice from the start so you do not migrate them next quarter.

lessons.title: Dynamic Cloud Voice is the current platform
lessons.summary: New trunks start there. Moving an old trunk means allow lists, Amazon root CAs, TLS ciphers, and a toggle.
paras: The DCVP article says to test a new trunk before you move production. Migration is not only a checkbox. You add the egress IP ranges to the carrier or SBC allow list, import Amazon root CAs so the far end trusts the BYOC endpoints, and confirm the TLS cipher list. Then you enable the high-capacity outbound platform on the trunk, and you point the far end’s SIP targets at the new ingress addresses.

The article warns that the Genesys-side toggle is the easy half. The remote SIP endpoint is the hard half. Change the allow list before you flip production, and keep a tested trunk beside the old one until inbound and outbound both complete.
lessons.uncertainty: Copy the IP ranges and cipher names from the current DCVP article. They are operational data and this lab does not duplicate them, because a stale copy would be worse than a link.

lessons.title: Number plans classify what people dial
lessons.summary: A site can hold 200 plans. DIDs do not need one for basic routing. Emergency, extension, and 988 already exist as defaults.
paras: Default classifications in the number-plan article include Emergency (911 and 933 in the United States and Canada, 142 in Switzerland), Extension for 4 to 6 digits, National, International, a regex Network plan, and Suicide Prevention, which routes 988 to +18002738255. Match types include digit length, E.164 list, inter-country, intra-country, number list, and regular expression. Intra-country and inter-country normalize to E.164. Digit length and E.164 lists do not.

You can normalize more than once as a number passes through plans. The product includes a call simulator. Use it. A custom classification is just a name you invent for a group of numbers. The lab’s number desk imitates these rules. It is not that simulator.

lessons.title: Watch the trunk, not only the flow
lessons.summary: When audio fails and Architect Insights still shows runs, the trunk is the next object.
paras: Monitor cloud media resources is the documented page for watching the cloud media your trunks use. A flow that transfers to ACD can be healthy while RTP is not. SIP responses tell you whether signaling completed. They do not tell you that the caller can hear the agent.

Pair that page with the carrier’s view of the same call. If Genesys shows the trunk up and the carrier shows the INVITE rejected, you are looking at policy on the far end: ACL, TLS trust, or a number the carrier will not route. The DCVP migration exists because those far-end checks are easy to miss.

lessons.title: Genesys Cloud Voice is the other door
lessons.summary: If Genesys is the carrier, you buy numbers in a region that offers voice, and emergency is part of that product story rather than your trunk.
paras: The Voice regions article lists where Genesys Cloud Voice operates and where it does not. Country tables restrict DID, toll-free, domestic, and international calling. FedRAMP is US-only for those services. The European Sovereign region does not extend its sovereignty promise to calls that leave the boundary.

Choosing GCV does not delete a BYOC design you already have. It does mean you must not assume the GCV emergency record follows a BYOC number. The overview’s CX 1 voice features, including campaigns and callbacks, are available on either carrier model. The carrier model changes who you call when a number will not complete.
